intro: New accounts clerks combine customer service with careful paperwork, a mix that banking and sales value. The closest of the 25 careers below is Tellers, with a 91% skill match, but Loan Officers are also 84% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $76,690, which is 61% more than the $47,670 clerks earn.
why_it_works: Opening an account means checking identity, explaining products and catching errors before they become problems. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.38 out of 5 for this job and social perceptiveness at 3.25. Collections, lending and financial sales draw on the same habits. Many matches need no new schooling. The gaps are negotiation, financial planning and managing resources, which lending and advising jobs use every day.
tips: Ask your bank about loan officer trainee roles; many promote from branch staff.
Sales representatives of services earn $69,990, which is 47% more, with no extra degree.
Earn a basic banking or lending certificate to show you are ready for financial sales.

faq.q: What jobs can former new accounts clerks do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Tellers (91%), Bill and Account Collectors (86%) and sales representatives of services (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Tellers earn $43,030, which is 10% less than the $47,670 median for new accounts clerks, so a lateral move rarely raises pay.

faq.q: Which careers for new accounts clerks pay more?
faq.a: 20 of the 25 matches pay more. Financial Managers earn $166,570 (249% more), Personal Financial Advisors $105,070 (120% more) and Insurance Underwriters $81,370 (71% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. All three usually need a bachelor's degree and some experience.

faq.q: Do new accounts clerks need a degree to change careers?
faq.a: For some paths. 18 of the 25 matches need no more education than clerks already have, but lending and advising roles usually need a bachelor's degree. In the closest match, 73% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent.

faq.q: What skills should new accounts clerks learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing materials, negotiation, managing financial resources and systems evaluation. Coordination already rates 3.12 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so learning to negotiate and analyze money is the main step toward lending.
